description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Aaron Donald expects to play Monday night against the Giants.
items.impact: According to head coach Sean McVay, at the start of this week, Donald was still uncertain to play Monday night. Donald made it known after Friday's practice session that he intends to be in action. The future Hall of Famer has not appeared in an NFL game since December 31, 2023.
items.title: Aaron Donald plans to play in Week 2

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Lukas Van Ness (concussion) is questionable for Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
items.impact: The Packers are uncertain whether or not Van Ness will play on Sunday, as he has yet receive full clearance from the NFL's concussion protocols. His absence would mean a weaker defensive front this week in a matchup against Breece Hall and the Jets.
items.title: Lukas Van Ness (concussion) questionable for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) is listed as questionable to play in Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
items.impact: A knee injury may leave Bako-Bewele sidelined on Sunday, as he is officially considered questionable heading into the weekend. Aaron Banks (knee) is also uncertain to play, so Green Bay's offensive line may be much weaker than usual if both of those guys are ruled out ahead of game time.
items.title: Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) listed questionable for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Aaron Banks (knee) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
items.impact: Banks has yet to make his season debut due to a knee injury, and it's threatening to leave him sidelined for another game on Sunday. Green Bay is dealing with multiple offensive line injuries right now, so they could be weaker than usual against the Jets this week.
items.title: Aaron Banks (knee) officially questionable for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Max Melton (ankle) is considered questionable for Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks.
items.impact: The Cardinals may be without a key defender on Sunday, as Melton is considered questionable to play due to his ankle injury. His absence would make life easier for Drew Lock, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and Seattle's offense as a whole this week.
items.title: Max Melton (ankle) considered questionable for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Tory Horton (hamstring) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: There was never much doubt surrounding Horton's availability for Week 2, but he has now received official clearance and will be available to suit up against the Cardinals. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him for the foreseeable future, however.
items.title: Tory Horton (hamstring) without injury designation for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Cooper Kupp (back) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: The veteran wideout was limited at practice earlier in the week due to a back injury, but he is over it now and carries no injury designation heading into the weekend. He doesn't project to be a good fantasy option in this matchup, however, especially with Drew Lock set to start at quarterback for the Seahawks this week.
items.title: Cooper Kupp (back) off injury report for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: Emmanwori was not able to play in Seattle's season opener last week, but he may make his season debut on Sunday, as he is officially considered questionable to play at this point. His return would provide a nice boost to this already-elite defense in a divisional matchup against the Cardinals.
items.title: Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) officially questionable for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Jordan Whittington (quad) was added to the injury report as a non-participant on Friday.
items.impact: Whittington is at risk of being sidelined in Week 2 after missing Friday's practice due to a quad injury of some kind. Puka Nacua (hip) is also at risk of being sidelined now, so fantasy managers should pay close attention to updates about the health of these two receivers prior to Monday night's game.
items.title: Jordan Whittington (quad) added to injury report Friday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Puka Nacua (hip) was added to the injury report as a non-participant at practice on Friday.
items.impact: Nacua is a new addition to the injury report, being listed with a hip injury of some kind that left him sidelined from practice on Friday. This is a situation that fantasy managers should be closely monitoring heading into the weekend because it could lead to him being limited or sidelined against the Giants on Monday night, which would be devastating for many managers relying on him for a big game at the end of the week.
items.title: Puka Nacua (hip) doesn't practice Friday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Eddy Pineiro (illness) is uncertain to play in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: The veteran kicker is officially considered questionable to play heading into the weekend. He is dealing with a mildly serious illness right now that has left him sidelined from practice all week, and it's unclear whether or not he will be ready to go in time for the team's matchup against the Dolphins, which would make them need to determine who will take his place prior to kickoff.
items.title: Eddy Pineiro (illness) uncertain to play Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Kaelon Black (groin) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: The rookie was added to the injury report due to a groin issue on Thursday and will officially be questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Dolphins. He was quite involved in San Francisco's season opener last week, so his absence would likely lead to Christian McCaffrey seeing a supermajority of touches for the team in Week 2.
items.title: Kaelon Black (groin) questionable to play Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Kyle Juszczyk (finger) will be available for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: The 49ers will have their star fullback for Sunday's game against Miami. He won't have any fantasy relevance himself but should help open things up for RB Christian McCaffrey in this favorable matchup.
items.title: Kyle Juszczyk (finger) available for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: George Kittle (Achilles) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: As expected, Kittle carries no injury designation heading into the weekend and will be available to play against the Dolphins. It seems likely that he will continue to be limited in some capacity, though it looks like the 49ers are planning on ramping his workload up more and more each week moving forward.
items.title: George Kittle (Achilles) good to go for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Alec Pierce (heel) will be good to go for Sunday night's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Pierce missed Indianapolis' practice on Thursday, but it looks like that was just for injury maintenance, as he was back and a full participant for them at practice on Friday. He carries no injury designation heading into the weekend and will play on Sunday night, although it remains quite possible that he will continue to have minor limitations while the team ramps his workload back up.
items.title: Alec Pierce (heel) good to go for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Anthony Richardson Sr. (groin) will be active for Sunday night's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Richardson is going to be active for the Colts on Sunday night, so his groin injury is likely considered nothing more than a minor issue at this point. He will continue to serve as the QB2 for this team behind Daniel Jones.
items.title: Anthony Richardson Sr. (groin) active for Week 2

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) is set to play in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: Neither of DeJean's injuries are serious at this point and he goes into the weekend without an injury designation. He will continue to play a big role on Philadelphia's defense moving forward, assuming he suffers no setbacks with his recovery.
items.title: Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) set to play Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Jonathan Greenard (pec) won't play play in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: The veteran edge rusher is going to be out this week, despite taking part at practice all week. He should return to the lineup and provide a nice boost to Philly's pass rush sometime in the near future.
items.title: Jonathan Greenard (pec) won't play Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Jalen Carter (wrist) will be available to play in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: Philadelphia's defense gets some good news ahead of Sunday's game, with Carter receiving full clearance to play against the Titans. He should continue to be a game-wrecker in what projects to be an easy matchup against Tennessee's low-powered offense.
items.title: Jalen Carter (wrist) available to play Sunday

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Jets signed fourth-round DL Darrell Jackson Jr. to his rookie deal.
items.impact: Jackson will compete for an immediate role on the Jets defensive line.
items.title: Darrell Jackson Jr. signs rookie deal with Jets

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Daron Payne (knee) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: Payne now has full clearance to play in Sunday's game against the Cowboys, which was to be expected after he was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday. Look for his presence to make a positive impact on Washington's defensive front in this matchup and beyond.
items.title: Daron Payne (knee) cleared to play Sunday

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Ladd McConkey (ribs) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders due to a rib injury.
items.impact: McConkey was a DNP Wednesday and Thursday but got back on the practice field Friday. His chances to play are more on the slim side, but if he plays, you need to start him against this Raiders defense. If he sits, Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris are next in line for targets.
items.title: Ladd McConkey (ribs) questionable for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Javon Kinlaw (back) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
items.impact: Kinlaw returned to practice on Friday and will officially be questionable to play in Washington's matchup against Dallas on Sunday. Their defensive front will be a little short on depth if he is ruled out ahead of kickoff for this game.
items.title: Javon Kinlaw (back) officially questionable for Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Odafe Oweh (calf) will be available to play in Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: As expected, Oweh is going to be available to play through his minor calf injury on Sunday. The team will need him to step up and help anchor down the defensive front in what projects to be a tough matchup against the Cowboys.
items.title: Odafe Oweh (calf) available to play Sunday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Jaylin Lane (groin) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: A groin injury left Lane limited at practice all week, but it's not a serious issue and won't affect his availability for Sunday's game against Dallas. He doesn't project to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, however.
items.title: Jaylin Lane (groin) good to go for Sunday

title: Fantasy Player News
